front:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production modular 2D cutout armour parts atlas for an isometric action RPG, NOT animation frames and NOT assembled people.
Input image: reference ONLY for the severe dark painterly ordinary steel armour finish, realistic adult proportions and small game-sprite readability. Create new matching Ward armour as disjoint parts.
Primary request: exactly FIFTEEN separate armour segments of ONE coherent knight set, all FRONT-RIGHT three-quarter view, orthographic elevated camera looking down 25 degrees. A narrow ridged CLOSED ordinary steel visor helmet; segmented breastplate; metal tassets; compact cuffs; pointed sabatons. Blackened charcoal steel, worn muted silver edges, tiny brass rivets, upper-left soft light. Entirely metal, no exposed skin, no cloth. Same scale for ALL parts, as if separated from one 700px-tall assembled adult knight.
Layout: 1024x1024 transparent canvas, 4 columns x4 rows of equal 256x256 cells, exactly one isolated part per occupied cell. Keep substantial transparent padding; absolutely no labels or grid. Put proximal joint near each cell centre x128,y70; parts hang DOWN vertically in neutral anatomical pose. Parts are NOT to fill cells equally: head height ~110px; torso height ~185px width170px; pelvis height~100px width150px; upper arms length115px width65px; forearms length105px width50px; hands length55px width44px; thighs length155px width70px; greaves length155px width55px; feet length90px width55px. Each cell part wholly contained and detached from all other cells.
ROW1 left-to-right: 1 helmet with short neck ring ONLY, no torso; 2 torso breastplate with neck collar and waist overlap lip ONLY, NO shoulders, arms, head, pelvis; 3 pelvis belt and overlapping metal tassets ONLY, NO thighs; 4 NEAR upper arm with shoulder pauldron and short lower elbow overlap collar, NO forearm or hand.
ROW2: 5 FAR upper arm with pauldron; 6 NEAR forearm bracer with elbow cup at top and wrist cuff below, no hand; 7 FAR forearm bracer; 8 NEAR empty closed metal gauntlet, relaxed grip around imaginary weapon, no weapon.
ROW3: 9 FAR empty closed metal gauntlet; 10 NEAR thigh armour with rounded hip interface and knee overlap lip; 11 FAR thigh armour; 12 NEAR greave with knee cup at top and ankle overlap at bottom, no foot.
ROW4: 13 FAR greave; 14 NEAR pointed plate sabaton foot; 15 FAR sabaton foot; 16 EMPTY transparent cell.
Near means viewer-facing right arm/leg of the knight; far means his opposite arm/leg; both have correct subtly different projected forms. All long limb segments oriented mostly downward, not posed bent. Metal disk interfaces and overlapping lips designed to hide joints during skeletal articulation. The full set must reassemble seamlessly; no fake human flesh interior.
Actual transparent alpha background; no opaque black/white/checkerboard; no shadows, floor, glow, text, labels, weapons, cape, shield, extra parts or assembled figure. Consistent painterly rendering, not vector icons, not cartoon. This is ordinary conventional full plate, NOT mythical seamless Warplate.
